clue.text: Heartily congratulating rugby players getting a round ahead

blocks.note: backs are the rugby players behind the scrum
lapping a rival in a race means getting a whole circuit in front of them

explanation.surface: A rugby team happily celebrates as its players pull a round ahead of the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping someone's back is a hearty gesture of praise, so the adjective describes effusive congratulation.

clue.text: Put sole initially in footwear for lift

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
putting one thing in another places it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a boot is a piece of footwear
the opening letter of sole

explanation.surface: Advice to slip an insole into a shoe to gain some height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' belongs to the shoe in the surface, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is an upward push or a raise, the same as a lift as a noun.

clue.text: Knight cold and hot over quivering Valerie

indicators.note: something quivering is shaking about, so the name's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the seven letters of Valerie rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight blows hot and cold over a trembling woman named Valerie.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' means the C and H sit above the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is the French title for a knight, used for members of some orders of knighthood.

clue.text: Modern painting restorers are concerned with this

definitions.text: painting restorers are concerned with this

blocks.note: first meaning: the most advanced, up to date

blocks.clueFragment: painting restorers are concerned with this
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: the condition a piece of art is in

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the phrase word by word: restorers care about the condition of the artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the latest technology, so it works as an adjective for modern things.

clue.text: Look — a penny on fruit

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for a penny
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone points out a coin lying on top of a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is the verb, as in 'you look tired', not a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to seem, the same verb sense as look in 'it looks fine'.

clue.text: I, perhaps, fix declaration

blocks.note: the word I is an example of a pronoun
to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: A first person speaker settles on a formal statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it stands for the word itself, a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal, authoritative statement, a synonym of declaration.

clue.text: Fanatic beheaded king

indicators.note: losing the head means the word drops its top letter

blocks.note: Cnut, also Canute, was an eleventh-century king of England

explanation.surface: A zealot has chopped off a monarch's head.
explanation.walkthrough: CNUT is the usual modern spelling of King Canute; dropping its C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is an informal word for an enthusiast or obsessive, as in a fitness nut.

clue.text: Finish after Friday, mate

indicators.note: after sends the word for finish behind the day's abbreviation

blocks.note: FRI is the calendar abbreviation for Friday
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Someone tells a pal they will finish the job after Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British for a companion or pal.

clue.text: Work taking a long time — Parsifal, perhaps

blocks.note: OP, short for opus, is a numbered musical work
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A grumble that Wagner's Parsifal takes ages to sit through.
explanation.walkthrough: Parsifal is notoriously long, about four hours, so the surface is a fair complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Wagner's last music drama, so it is one example of the genre.

clue.text: One scheming young wizard, about fifty

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of the novels
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A boy wizard is plotting something, and he is around fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: The L sits inside POTTER, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter is a person who devises secret plans, i.e. a schemer.

clue.text: Thanks on being fed last of the drink

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word
something being fed takes something else inside it

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks
the final letter of the

explanation.surface: Saying thank you after being given the last of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the hot beverage made by infusing leaves, a standard drink.

clue.text: English and American work at key complex

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
labor is the American spelling of labour, work
taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: British and US staff working at a key, intricate project.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective means intricate and detailed, a synonym of complex.

clue.text: How to make neat see-saw or yo-yo?

indicators.note: to make one word from another is to rework its letters, here in reverse

blocks.note: the instruction for turning one word into another: change it
the letters that, once changed, produce neat

explanation.surface: A question about how to tidy up a see-saw or yo-yo.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer read as 'alter NATE' is an instruction that produces neat.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to swing back and forth repeatedly, which is what to see-saw or to yo-yo means as a verb.

clue.text: Short of French cheese, only one piece of fromage

indicators.note: a single piece of the word means just its first letter is kept

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
the opening letter of fromage

explanation.surface: A cheese shop runs short of Brie, with just one piece left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' looks like a phrase, but 'Short' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means lasting a short time or concise, a synonym of short.

clue.text: Earlier tidal wave carrying energy and force

indicators.note: a thing carrying something holds it inside itself

blocks.note: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river, like the Severn bore

F is the symbol for force

explanation.surface: An earlier tidal surge that swept along with tremendous energy and power.
explanation.walkthrough: E and F go inside BORE, between BO and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Before as an adverb means at a previous time, a synonym of earlier.

clue.text: Eminent lecturer returned around first half of term

around means one piece is wrapped about the other
only the front half of the word is kept, its opening two letters

the front half of term

explanation.surface: A distinguished academic came back around the middle of the first term.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge; here half the letters of term are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known and distinguished, so it is a synonym of eminent.

clue.text: In gospel truth this reptile goes backwards

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the following words
going backwards means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A wry remark that this slow animal, honestly, moves in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of gospel into truth, and are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a shelled reptile, so it is one kind of the class named.

clue.text: Distant US home rebuilt — a place in the country

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form

blocks.note: far means distant
the six letters of us home rearranged

explanation.surface: A remote American house gets rebuilt as a rural retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse is the dwelling on a farm, so it is a home in rural surroundings.

clue.text: Bone carried by tribesman

indicators.note: carried by means held within the next word

blocks.note: the letters lie just after the opening T

explanation.surface: A tribesman carries a bone, perhaps as a tool or ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib is one of the curved bones of the chest.

clue.text: Bathroom fitting I'd bet needs throwing out

indicators.note: throwing something about scatters it, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the five letters of I'd bet rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wagers that an old bathroom fixture has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin for washing, plumbed into some bathrooms.

clue.text: Begin once more to relax with music, say

blocks.note: to rest is to relax
music is an example of an art

explanation.surface: Taking a break with some music before starting again.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start again, so it replaces begin once more as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Almost miss out winter sports equipment

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to skip is to miss out

explanation.surface: Someone nearly misses out on the gear for a winter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is the long runner strapped to the boot for gliding on snow.

clue.text: First pair of elephants together with antelope

indicators.note: a first pair means the opening two letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening two letters of elephants
and means together with

explanation.surface: Two elephants lead the way, with an antelope alongside, as on safari.

clue.text: Abuse met at minster, unfortunately

blocks.note: the twelve letters of met at minster rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suffered abuse when they met up at a cathedral church.
explanation.walkthrough: A minster is a large church, such as York Minster.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistreatment means cruel or unfair handling of someone, a synonym of abuse as a noun.
